text:
Hanna G: Quick question - post-canary we saw a few false positives in redaction_leakage alerts. Signal seems noisy when tenants have large attachments. Ideas?

Liam O: We should separate attachments from text-based redaction metrics. Create `redaction_leakage_text` and `redaction_leakage_attachments`. Alert thresholds differ.

Noah W: Also add content-size buckets to the metric labels: small/medium/large. Large attachments should be excluded from the heatmap by default unless user opts in.

security-bot: Incident 2026-03-18T09:02Z: redaction_leakage alert (tenant: acme-corp) auto-escalated.

Hanna G: For the immediate fix, I propose we mute attachment-based leakage for 24h while we investigate and add a suppression label in the alert metadata. Ops can unmute via the console.

Liam O: Long-term: change the redaction_score to be weighted by token density and attachment_score. We can compute `adjusted_redaction_score = 0.6*text_score + 0.4*attachment_score` (weights adjustable).

Noah W: We'll need a migration plan for historical alerts. Suggest backfill `attachment_score` for last 7 days into telemetry store so teams can re-evaluate prior alerts.

Hanna G: I'll add a note to the runbook: if attachment-based alerts spike, mute and open a ticket to backfill attachment_score. Also add a console toggle to "include attachments in heatmap".

devops-bot: patch 2026-03-19T02:00Z rolled: redaction_alerts: add suppression_label `attachment_noise`.
